text.text: Everything we know, in one place. Find a policy, read the news, meet the teams. If a page looks out of date, tell its owner.
The wiki is only useful if people trust it. Three habits keep it honest.
The owner answers questions about it and reviews it twice a year.
Every page has a review date
When the date passes, the page shows as Expired until the owner reads it again and moves the date forward.
Assume the reader started this week. Say what a thing is before saying how to do it.
Share this page with every new hire on their first morning.
Laptop, accounts and password manager set up
Meet your manager and your team lead
Read the returns and time-off policies
Shadow a customer care shift for an hour
Walk the warehouse floor with the manager
Book a check-in with People and culture
Pages come due for review on these dates. Owners: open your pages and confirm they are still true.
Open the Review due this week list on Monday.
Read each page you own. If it is still right, press Mark verified and set a new review date.
If it is wrong, fix it first, then verify. A page nobody verified stays Expired and shows in Needs review.
Aim for a review date three to six months out. Policies that change rarely can go a year.
Everyone who owns a wiki page or leads a team appears here. Add new hires on their first day so owners can be picked from the list.
